newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $1 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $1 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices early Wednesday were steady to $1.00 per cwt higher, with most advances in the eastern Corn Belt where it has not rained yet, livestock dealers said.

Farmers in Illinois, Indiana and Ohio were busy planting, leaving little time to sell hogs. Despite slaughter cutbacks at a number of plants, packers were forced to compete for tight available hog supplies. Hog runs in Iowa and southern Minnesota rose slightly in areas where rain delayed fieldwork.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hogs sold steady at $54.50 to $55.00 in the country and up to $57.00 at plants.

Illinois hogs sold $0.50 to $1.00 higher at $56.50 to $57.50 in the country and $58.00 to $58.50 at plants. Several packers paid premiums for top quality hogs of $1.00 to $2.00 over Tuesday's top price of $56.50 reported by USDA, sources there said.

Indiana hogs sold $0.50 higher at $54.50 to $55.00 in the country and $56.50, possibly $57.00, at plants. Prices could go higher as the day progressed if competition for hogs intensifies, buyers said.
Ohio hogs sold $0.50 to $1.00 higher at $55.00 to $56.00 in the country and $57.00 at plants, dealers said.
